effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive quantitative percentages and qualitative process-tracing findings only; no inferential statistical test, confidence interval, or p-value is reported. Note that table cells for Cuadros 1-10 are omitted in the XML-JATS4R PDF rendering, so all extracted percentages come strictly from the main text.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive mixed-methods findings (no inferential regression estimate reported): Under Santa Fe Law 11220/94, the provincial state utility (ASSA) serves only 15 populous localities (59% of provincial population) with subsidies covering 40% of operating costs, whereas the remaining 347 localities (including 126 cooperatives across 124 localities, where 79% [98 cases] supply only water and 21% [26 cases] supply water and sewerage) receive no mandatory provincial operating subsidies and cooperatives face dual municipal and ENRESS control. Between 2010 and 2018, cooperative-served localities increased public-network water coverage from 80% to 92% (remaining 3 percentage points below ASSA-served localities, which had 90% in 2010) and sewerage coverage from 22% to 37% (compared with 50% in 2010 and 68% in 2018 in ASSA-served localities). Across 115 coded actions (2010-2011), 68% of provincial executive actions were non-confrontational (61% tied to discretionary, discontinuous minor water-quality works without systematic planning or sewerage expansion), while political conflict over stripping ENRESS of tariff-regulatory authority stalled legislative reform of Law 11220/94.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 3-5, Section II; PDF pp. 13-18, Section IV.4-IV.5 and Section V

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 per CODEBOOK.md §9 design ceiling for non-experimental/mixed-methods case studies; assigned 2 because the study directly observes and documents the statutory, regulatory, planning, financial, and political mechanisms operating through Law 11220/94, dual ENRESS/local oversight, discretionary infrastructure works, and legislative deadlock via key-informant interviews, legislative bills, and event reconstruction.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 2-6, Sections I-II; PDF pp. 12-18, Sections IV-V

mechanism_flags.comment: Law 11220/94 restricts mandatory provincial provision and 40% operating subsidies to a 15-locality service area (ELIGIBILITY, service_area); small localities and cooperatives lack technical planning teams and the Provincial Strategic Plan omitted sewerage (planning); cooperatives face dual municipal/ENRESS oversight complicating tariff-increase procedures and lack subsidies (BURDEN, fees, procedural_steps); provincial works in cooperative localities were discretionary and discontinuous, and bills proposed vulnerable-user subsidies (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, discretion); ENRESS water-quality enforcement, public hearings, user/provider complaints, multi-tier fragmentation, and executive-regulator-legislative partisan conflict stalled statutory reform (ENFORCEMENT, complaint, participation, institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination).

study_design.comment: Described by the authors as an exploratory empirical study reconstructing social processes from the written press (quantitative descriptive coding of 115 actions into actor/conflict/problem variables), complemented by qualitative key-informant interviews, institutional/legislative document analysis, and descriptive comparison of census (2010) and regulator (2016, 2019) coverage statistics.
study_design.value: Exploratory mixed-methods case study combining quantitative descriptive newspaper event analysis (process reconstruction of coded actions) and administrative/census coverage data with qualitative key-informant interviews and institutional/legislative document analysis

evidence_quotes.quote: la provincia de Santa Fe (Argentina) se caracteriza por poseer un sistema discriminatorio de gestión de los SAS, en el cual el Estado provincial solamente se hace cargo de proveer el servicio de forma directa a las 15 localidades más pobladas, con tarifas subsidiadas e inversión pública en infraestructura.

debido a que el poder de concesión está a cargo de los Estados locales, las cooperativas, a diferencia de las comunas y municipios, están sujetas a un doble control: por parte de las autoridades locales y por parte del Ente Regulador de los Servicios Sanitarios (ENRESS). Esto diﬁculta los trámites necesarios que debe hacer una cooperativa para poder funcionar, como por ejemplo el pedido de aumento de tarifa.

evidence_quotes.criterion: effect_estimate (2010 baseline water and sanitation access)
evidence_quotes.quote: Las poblaciones donde el prestador principal es una cooperativa, tienen un promedio de acceso a agua por red pública del 80% y del 22% en cloacas. Esta situación contrasta con la realidad de las localidades que son provistas por la empresa estatal, donde el promedio de acceso a agua por red pública es del 90% y el de acceso a cloacas es del 50%.
De las 48 noticias seleccionadas para los años 2010 y 2011 se identiﬁcaron 115 acciones.

Para completar el período de estudio y tener una mayor comprensión de los tipos de relaciones predominantes, los conﬂictos y los problemas que originan las acciones realizamos entrevistas a actores clave (funcionarios políticos, personal técnico y miembros de organizaciones sociales), analizamos documentos institucionales y relevamos los datos de cobertura de agua y cloacas provistos por el Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas y Censos (INDEC) y por el ENRESS.

Con relación a la cobertura de cloacas la desigualdad es aún más acentuada. Si bien las cooperativas han logrado ampliar la cobertura, pasando de un 22 a un 37%, siguen estando muy por debajo del nivel de cobertura de las localidades provistas por ASSA, que era para el año 2018 de un 68%.
